parameters.name: bias
parameters.description: Constant acceleration offset `bias`. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: gain
parameters.description: Linear input gain `gain`. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: damp
parameters.description: Linear velocity damping coefficient `damp`. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: stiff
parameters.description: Multiplier `stiff` of the polynomial restoring function. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: fric
parameters.description: Baseline smooth friction amplitude `fric`. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Velocity regularization scale in `tanh(x1/width)`. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: soft
parameters.description: Cubic softening shape coefficient `soft`. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: asym
parameters.description: Even restoring correction coefficient in `asym*y**2`. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: fricLinear
parameters.description: Odd friction-amplitude correction in `fricLinear*y`. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: fricQuad
parameters.description: Even friction-amplitude correction in `fricQuad*y**2`. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: floor
parameters.description: Positive shape margin `floor` used in the tied fifth-order coefficient. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

parameters.name: fifth
parameters.description: Fifth-order restoring coefficient `fifth`, constrained by `fifth = soft**2/4+floor**2` to prevent a zero or negative symmetric restoring multiplier. Its value is on the supplied logged scale; physical units are not stated.

estimation.criterion: Sum of squared free-running output errors in `y`, excluding the initial row of each trajectory. Each rollout uses classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta at the supplied sampling period `0.01` s and holds `x2` constant within a sample. Simulated states are never reset to subsequent measurements. The training-only stage and final joint stage use the same criterion, because integrated output accuracy, rather than sampled derivative accuracy, is the requested use. The expression `dy = x1` is assumed from the essentially exact central-difference relation observed on interior rows and is not fitted.
estimation.data: Training stage: `data/train.csv`, all thirteen trajectories and all rows after the first row of each trajectory, with each initial logged pair `y`, `x1` used only as an initial condition. Final stage: the same rows plus `data/val.csv`, all three trajectories and all rows after their first rows. No test data were available or used. There are 4698 scored time samples across the two supplied files. Rows were equally weighted to match sample-wise output scoring; derivative columns were used in structural exploration but not in these final objectives. All listed trajectories were retained to test different cold-start conditions. Exact suffix overlaps were found: training trajectories 8 and 11 reproduce validation trajectory 1 from row 309 and validation trajectory 2 from row 209 respectively (zero-based row indices); training trajectories 9, 10, 12 and 13 reproduce training trajectories 1, 2, 3 and 4 from rows 309, 309, 209 and 209. Thus file-level validation is not an independent-experiment holdout. The final use of validation is explicit and its final error is in-sample.
estimation.method: Bounded nonlinear least squares, using the trust-region-reflective algorithm in `scipy.optimize.least_squares` (SciPy 1.18.1). This is direct output-error system identification: integration makes the objective nonlinear in all coefficients, so ordinary least squares cannot solve it. All fitted coefficients were optimized jointly in each of two stages. The polynomial coefficient `fifth` is not independently estimated: after both fits it is computed from `soft` and `floor` by its tie equation. All other parameters were fitted jointly. The training-only numeric starting vector in the coefficient order of the parameter rows was `[3, 28, 1.6, 112, 20, 0.15, -0.17, -2, -5, 4, 0.04]`, on the logged parameter scales (physical units unknown). These rounded exploratory starting values place the restoring strength, input gain and friction near the derivative-regression scale and avoid an unstable initial rollout. The final joint starting vector was the training-only estimate `[2.9464447876142574, 28.281093740934235, 1.5544950297539193, 114.30582249544753, 20.191857532703374, 0.12000000000275601, -0.17829033527367544, -0.20707700929522607, -4.759762017386083, 4.36561376445295, 0.05386695561121672]`, on those same scales, so it was warm-started rather than restarted randomly. The final bounds in this coefficient order were `[[-20.0, 5.0, 0.2, 50.0, 10.0, 0.12, -0.3, -10.0, -10.0, 0.0, 0.001], [20.0, 60.0, 5.0, 180.0, 35.0, 3.0, -0.05, 10.0, 10.0, 10.0, 0.2]]`, on those same scales. Positive damping, restoring strength and friction were bounded to select a dissipative model; wide remaining bounds limit poorly supported extrapolation. The training-only script is `fit_polynomial.py`; its starting shape uses the low-order sine expansion as a heuristic. The shape parameter bounds enforce negative cubic softening, positive fifth-order margin and nonnegative quadratic friction modulation. The width lower bound was chosen to avoid unresolved sharp friction transitions at the supplied sampling period. Both stages used `diff_step = 0.0001`, `x_scale = 'jac'`, `ftol = 1e-7`, `xtol = 1e-7`, `gtol = 1e-6`; these dimensionless optimizer settings were chosen for a reproducible local fit without demanding more precision than the logged resolution. Training evaluations were capped at `max_nfev = 140` for the trigonometric models and `max_nfev = 180` for the polynomial model; the final cap was `max_nfev = 180`. Two-point finite-difference Jacobians were used. No random search or random numbers were used; no seed applies. Bounds and starts are also recorded in `results/`. The optimizer is local and global optimality is not claimed. Method reference: T. F. Coleman and Y. Li, An Interior Trust Region Approach for Nonlinear Minimization Subject to Bounds, SIAM Journal on Optimization (1996), cited from memory without successful source verification. `final_fit.py` reproduces the final estimates from the saved training-only results; the cited stage scripts reproduce those warm starts.

discussion.family: Polynomial nonlinear state-space oscillator, a stabilized higher-order Duffing-type restoring model with smooth velocity saturation. Duffing's original cubic oscillator is described in G. Duffing, Erzwungene Schwingungen bei veraenderlicher Eigenfrequenz und ihre technische Bedeutung (1918); reference cited from memory without successful source verification. This candidate extends that mathematical family and does not assert a Duffing mechanical device.
discussion.interpretation: `dy = x1` is velocity-like kinematics. `bias+gain*x2` adds a constant and linear input drive. `-damp*x1` is linear damping. The restoring term `-stiff*(y+soft*y**3+fifth*y**5)` contains linear attraction, cubic softening and fifth-order stabilization. With `fifth = soft**2/4+floor**2`, its factor `1+soft*y**2+fifth*y**4` remains positive for every real coordinate, unlike a pure softening cubic outside its training range. The correction `asym*y**2` allows unequal positive/negative restoring magnitudes. The positive fitted quadratic amplitude `fric+fricLinear*y+fricQuad*y**2` multiplies the bounded odd function `tanh(x1/width)` to oppose velocity; `fricLinear` and `fricQuad` allow coordinate-dependent resistance. Each coefficient is empirical, with no known physical unit or component identification.
discussion.origin: Cubic restoring fits were substantially better than affine fits and competitive with sine fits. Rather than submit an unbounded softening cubic with spurious outside-range equilibria, I added a constrained fifth-order term; that constraint is an extrapolation safeguard chosen mathematically, not inferred as a physical law. I then used a purely polynomial first-state basis for restoring asymmetry and friction modulation, instead of the trigonometric basis used by the other candidates. `asym*y**2`, `fricLinear*y` and `fricQuad*y**2` were manually proposed to address sign-asymmetric large-coordinate residuals observed in the sine-plus-constant-friction fit. No automatic symbolic regression was run. All fitted terms were jointly estimated; their inclusion is judged by free-running output performance rather than derivative fit alone. Before the final joint refit, sample-weighted free-running `y` RMSE was `0.03534764` on training and `0.07567046` on validation, in unspecified `y` units. After the final refit these were `0.03711180` and `0.06970017` respectively, now both in-sample. Diagnostics in `residuals.py` compare sampled `dx1` residuals and free-running output residuals. Sampled derivative RMSE was `9.842610` on training and `16.334292` on validation, in unspecified derivative units. The final validation per-trajectory output RMSE vector was `[0.09383099778791351, 0.04064761864272886, 0.05489980549473038]` in unspecified `y` units. These diagnostics are not test results.
discussion.limitations: The physical system, units, measurement process, intended use and meaning of `x2` are not supplied. Numerical coefficients refer to the logged scales, not identified physical constants. Trigonometric arguments assume the numerical `y` coordinate is suitable for a dimensionless angle-like representation; no physical angle unit is asserted. The logged `x1` and `dx1` equal central finite differences of `y` and `x1` on interior rows, to numerical precision, and are quantized, so instantaneous derivatives are not independently measured. Identification cannot separate all measurement and dynamic effects. The observed training domain is approximately `-2.5133 <= y <= 2.5353`, `-20.1062 <= x1 <= 14.4513`, `-4.9452 <= x2 <= 3.9526`, all in unspecified logged units. Extrapolation outside this domain or beyond the supplied trajectory lengths is unvalidated. There are experiment-dependent residuals, notably validation trajectory 1, and exact train/validation suffix overlaps; neither file-level validation nor the final combined fit is a pristine independent test. This family does not assume coordinate periodicity and its high-degree restoring function grows rapidly outside the logged domain; RK4 stability outside that domain is not established. The fifth-order sign constraint is a chosen mathematical safeguard, not proof of global stability of the full asymmetric forced model. The smooth friction has no true sticking interval and can drift from logged nonzero rest coordinates. Several restoring and friction shape coefficients can trade off because trajectory coverage is limited; the velocity-scale bound is active.
